trajectory_messages.content:
Enhance the 'new-window' event in Electron to include referrer information. This will allow applications to forward the referrer context when handling new window requests, ensuring the proper Referer HTTP header is sent to the server.

*   Update the 'new-window' event emitted by `webContents`:
    *   Add a 'referrer' object as the 7th argument in the event callback.
    *   Ensure the callback signature is `(event, url, frameName, disposition, options, additionalFeatures, referrer)`.

*   Implement the 'referrer' object with the following properties:
    *   `url` (string): Set to the URL of the page that initiated the new window request.
    *   `policy` (string): Set to the applicable referrer policy. For standard HTTP pages opened via `target=_blank` links, use 'no-referrer-when-downgrade'.

*   Ensure that when a new window is opened via a link with `target=_blank`:
    *   The HTTP Referer header on subsequent requests from the new window is set to the originating page's URL.

*   Modify the following files:
    *   `lib/browser/api/web-contents.js`: Emit the 'new-window' event with the updated signature.
    *   `docs/api/structures/referrer.md`: Document the structure of the 'referrer' object.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory. The verification system will apply test patches automatically. Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Here's what I found regarding the Electron `new-window` event, the Referrer object, and the relevant pull request affecting `web-contents.js`:

## The Referrer Object

The `Referrer` object in Electron has two properties: url (string) - the HTTP Referrer URL, and policy (string) - which can be default, unsafe-url, no-referrer-when-downgrade, no-referrer, origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin or strict-origin. The policy values follow the Referrer-Policy specification.

## How the Referrer is used with new windows

When a new window is opened, the referrer is passed to the new window. This may or may not result in the Referer header being sent, depending on the referrer policy.

The `new-window` event itself is emitted when the page requests to open a new window for a url. It could be requested by window.open or an external link like `<a target='_blank'>`. By default a new BrowserWindow will be created for the url. In this event handler, disposition (String) can be default, foreground-tab, background-tab, new-window, save-to-disk and other; options (Object) are used for creating the new BrowserWindow; additionalFeatures (String[]) are the non-standard features given to window.open(); and referrer (Referrer) is the referrer that will be passed to the new window.

## The Pull Request (#16623) affecting web-contents.js

The relevant pull request is **PR #16623**, titled "fix: handle window.open() in web-contents.js" by ckerr. The description explains its purpose: to move window.open() handling from browser-window.js to web-contents.js.

The key code change involved an event handler where the webContents listens on '-new-window' with parameters (event, url, frameName, disposition, additionalFeatures, postData, referrer), then emits 'ELECTRON_GUEST_WINDOW_MANAGER_INTERNAL_WINDOW_OPEN' passing along event, url, referrer, frameName, disposition, options, additionalFeatures, and postData.

This PR was related to issue #16621 and CC'd codebytere, MarshallOfSound, and alexeykuzmin.

## Summary

I enhanced the `new-window` event to carry a `referrer` object, threading it through the window-opening pipeline so the `Referer` HTTP header is sent by newly opened windows.

### `lib/browser/api/web-contents.js` (primary)
Added a `-new-window` handler in `_init` (the internal native event fires only for browser/offscreen contents). It synthesizes the referrer from the originating page and forwards it into the window-open pipeline:
```js
const referrer = {
  url: this.getURL(),
  policy: 'no-referrer-when-downgrade'
}
```
This is where the `referrer` for `target=_blank` links originates — `this.getURL()` is the page that initiated the request.

### `lib/browser/api/browser-window.js`
Removed the now-relocated `-new-window` handler (it would otherwise double-fire), and passed a default referrer through the native `window.open` (`-add-new-contents`) path.

### `lib/browser/guest-window-manager.js`
- `INTERNAL_WINDOW_OPEN` handler now receives `referrer` and emits the public event with the required 7-argument signature:
  `event.sender.emit('new-window', event, url, frameName, disposition, options, additionalFeatures, referrer)`
- `createGuest` accepts `referrer` and sets `loadOptions.httpReferrer = referrer.url`, so the new window sends the proper `Referer` header.
- The `window.open` (`WINDOW_OPEN`) path passes a `{ url: '', policy: 'default' }` referrer.

### Docs
- `docs/api/structures/referrer.md` — new `Referrer` structure (`url`, `policy`).
- `docs/api/web-contents.md` — documented `referrer` as the new argument on the `new-window` event.

All three JS files pass `node --check`. I did not touch anything under `tests/`.

One note: the native `loadURL` binding in this snapshot reads `httpReferrer` as a plain URL string (it always applies the default Chromium referrer policy), so the header's URL is honored but the `policy` field of the object is only surfaced to JS listeners of the `new-window` event — it isn't enforced natively without a C++ change, which was out of scope per the instructions.
